images.title: Under the Door
images.prompt: Painterly cinematic still, an old 1920s river hotel at night, 1970s paranoid-thriller restraint, opaque gouache brush drag, practical lamps only, bottle-green cloth wallpaper, worn varnish, thumb-polished brass, tobacco-amber lamplight against river-grey light, brown-black shadow, soft film grain. Five in the morning in a very long, very narrow hidden service passage, camera centred looking straight down its length, symmetrical one-point perspective, no people. Along the left wall a row of six narrow dark doors, each with a small round unlit brass peephole rose. Nothing hangs on the walls. On the floor, a single blank dark blue-black sheet of carbon paper lies half slid under the nearest door, only its corner showing on the floorboards. Dead centre at the far end of the passage, a seventh plain door whose peephole glows: one tiny bright point of amber light, the only warm light in the picture. Thin river-grey dawn from high windows on the right, wall lamps off, threadbare runner, dark wainscot. Emptied, waiting. The lower quarter is quiet dark floorboards. No notices, no posters, no printed paper, no text, no lettering, no watermark, no logo.
images.needs_review: Retry kept (first try had a printed notice with pseudo-lettering on the wall and no lit far door). Still off: blank picture frames on the walls, a ceiling lamp lit at the top edge, and the carbon sheet reads as a large dark mat rather than a sheet corner under the door.

Dawn in a double-height marble hotel lobby, a high wide view looking down from the mezzanine, all figures tiny and far below. Three small figures walk away from us in a row toward the revolving door: a hotel guest in a plain overcoat carrying one small suitcase, flanked by two uniformed police officers seen from behind, one on each side, unhurried, nobody touching anybody; the guest looks back over one shoulder and up toward the camera, face too small and shadowed to read. Apart from them, alone at the reception desk on the right, a night clerk in a waistcoat faces the camera and raises a black telephone receiver high above his head toward the mezzanine, offering it to the viewer. Flat river-grey daylight through the revolving door, a brass chandelier still burning amber. The lower quarter is the calm dark varnished mezzanine rail and shadow. First grey light at a wet stone river wall behind a five-storey brick hotel, fog on the water. In the left foreground a tall thin man in his thirties in a long grey raincoat and flat cap, seen only from behind, stands at the wall, hands in pockets, facing the river, not the building. Across the upper frame the hotel's fourth floor: a row of six tall guest windows, five lit, each a different colour of lamp, white, blue, yellow, pale screen glow and red-shaded amber, and one window among them dark. At the end of the row one small narrow window still glows green-amber, a desk lamp left on. A sodium streetlamp fading orange in the fog. The lower quarter is calm wet cobbles. images.needs_review: Not retried. The hotel stands across the water, so the man faces the building, where the prompt has him facing the river and not the building; the green-amber window is on the floor below the row.
